lastDecision: Reject the current Cross-Asset Relative Strength 15m formulation. The relative-strength ranking produced only a very small positive gross spread, which was substantially below the assumed two-leg execution cost at every tested horizon. Do not integrate into Railway or the paper loop.
interpretation: The relative-strength ranking contains a weak positive gross spread, but the spread is far smaller than realistic two-leg costs.
The best tested horizon was 12h, with only +0.1183% average gross spread against 0.4% assumed pair cost.
Both the long-strongest and short-weakest legs remained negative after their individual cost allowance.
Hit rate remained below 50% at every horizon.
Longer holding periods reduced the loss but did not create a tradeable edge.
The 3000, 6000 and 12000 runs are nested samples and should not be treated as three independent validations.
knownProblems: Gross edge is too small relative to fees and execution costs
All tested horizons are negative after costs
All tested net medians are negative
Hit rate is below 50% at all horizons
Further regime or threshold tuning on the same sample would create overfitting risk
blockedChanges: Do not add this strategy to Railway
Do not add this strategy to the paper portfolio loop
Do not enable real trading or real orders
Do not use private exchange API keys
Do not lower assumed costs merely to make the result positive
Do not reverse the strategy solely because the net result is negative
Do not optimize lookbacks or regimes on the same March-July 2026 sample
Do not expand the universe to illiquid altcoins
nextResearch: Archive the current formulation as a failed cost-gate candidate
Keep the report as evidence of the completed test
Return to the strategy bank and choose a structurally different hypothesis
Prefer event-driven or slower regime strategies with larger expected movement relative to costs
